ukmt-pk-2025-03.title: Look at the blue triangles
ukmt-pk-2025-03.body:
On Larissa's pinwheel the two blue triangles are directly opposite each other. In wheels A and B they are not, so those are out.

Going clockwise, the pink triangle is immediately followed by a blue triangle. Of C, D, E only E has this.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-pk-2025-04.title: Draw the reflection
ukmt-pk-2025-04.body:
In the mirror the order of the digits is reversed and each digit is flipped. The 5 looks like a 2, the 2 looks like a 5, and the 0 looks like a 0. So the reflection reads $2505$.

The difference is $2505-2025=480$.

**Answer: (C) 480**

ukmt-pk-2025-04.title: Compare place by place
ukmt-pk-2025-04.body:
$2505$ and $2025$ have the same thousands digit and the same units digit. They differ in the hundreds ($5$ against $0$) and the tens ($0$ against $2$). So the difference is $500-20=480$.

**Answer: (C) 480**

ukmt-pk-2025-06.title: Join up the tracks
ukmt-pk-2025-06.body:
Follow each line across the foot-shaped hole and join the pieces on either side. Doing this, the lines crossing the foot make exactly the pattern shown in option B.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-pk-2025-08.title: Look at the second rod
ukmt-pk-2025-08.body:
The second rod has two triangles on the same side. In options A, B and D the rod with two triangles has them on different sides, so they are out. Option C needs a rod with a square and a triangle on different sides of the same rod, which Jorge does not have. Only E has two triangles on the same side, and the other two rods fit.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-pk-2025-14.title: Add the fold lines
ukmt-pk-2025-14.body:
Draw the two fold lines on the snowflake, one horizontal and one vertical through the middle. Each quarter of the snowflake is what the folded square looks like, and each quarter looks like the pattern in option B.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-pk-2025-15.title: Try each piece
ukmt-pk-2025-15.body:
Piece 4 fits neither hole. Turn piece 1 so that three squares are in a horizontal row: it fits the upper hole with the correct colouring (piece 3 fits the shape but not the colouring). Turn piece 5 so that three squares are in a vertical column: it fits the hole on the right with the correct colouring. Piece 2 would only fit after being reflected and then has the wrong colouring.

**Answer: (B) pieces 1 and 5**

ukmt-pk-2025-16.title: Count the squares
ukmt-pk-2025-16.body:
The longest side of a given piece is 6, so Bob's square has side at least 6 and at least $6\times6=36$ small squares. The three given pieces have $8+10+6=24$ squares, so the fourth has at least $36-24=12$. Both D and E have 12 squares. Trying them, only E (4 squares wide and 3 high) fits with the other three to make a $6\times6$ square.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-pk-2025-17.title: Colour from the known cube
ukmt-pk-2025-17.body:
The cube directly underneath the blue cube must be pink. Then the two cubes P and R of the bottom layer that touch that pink cube must be blue, and the cube Q touching both P and R must be pink. Continue along rows and columns, alternating the colours, to colour the whole pyramid. From above the result is option D.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-pk-2025-19.title: Compare tubes at the same level
ukmt-pk-2025-19.body:
Tubes 1, 2 and 3 have the same level, but tube 3 has the most balls (3 against 1 and 2), so it has the least water. Likewise tube 5 has more balls than tube 4, so tube 5 has less water than tube 4. The least water is in tube 3 or tube 5.

Pour everything from two copies of tube 3 (water and balls) into one tube: you get a tube that looks exactly like tube 5, with twice the water. So tube 5 has twice as much water as tube 3.

**Answer: (C) test tube 3**

ukmt-pk-2025-19.title: Think in volumes
ukmt-pk-2025-19.body:
Let one ball have volume $b$ and tube 3 hold total volume $V$ below its water level, so the water in tube 3 is $V-3b$. Tube 5 reaches level $2V$ and holds 6 balls, so its water is $2V-6b=2(V-3b)$. So tube 5 has twice as much water as tube 3, and tube 3 has the least.

**Answer: (C) test tube 3**
